notes: VCST-5028 cross-org member — TechFlow leg (org-maintainer); roles are org-scoped only (no global role)

VCST-5281 TWIN of MOM-001 — TechFlow leg (org-maintainer). A SECOND account in the SAME two orgs: OrganizationMembership rows are keyed on (userId, organizationId), so two accounts own independent rows and two parallel lanes can mutate status/lock without colliding.
VCST-5281 TWIN of MOM-002 — BuildRight leg (org-employee)

VCST-5281 SINGLE-org invitee (frontend lane). EXACTLY ONE membership row by design — the ABSENCE of a BuildRight row is load-bearing: the P0 trigger is a genuine FIRST-TIME invite into BuildRight, and an already-Invited membership is not re-invitable (only resendable). NEVER add a second org row to this account.

VCST-5281 SINGLE-org blocking-status subject (backend lane). EXACTLY ONE membership row, walked Approved -> Invited -> Rejected -> Deleted -> Approved by the test. Dedicated account so the walk never blocks another suite; separate from MOM-005 because the invite flow and the status walk run concurrently in different lanes.

VCST-5281 status representative — Invited (a BlockingStatus). Per-org OrganizationMembership.Status=Invited over a contact whose status is Approved, so a refusal is provably the PER-ORG override and not the contact global status. SINGLE-org by design: a second org would mask the refusal through the healthy-org fall-through path. DEDICATED account — an Invited membership blocks org sign-in, so this must never be pointed at a happy-path case. Not re-invitable (ReinvitableStatuses = Rejected, Deleted) — only resendable.

VCST-5281 status representative — Rejected (a BlockingStatus, and Reinvitable). Same single-org shape as MOM-007 over an Approved contact. Use for the rejected-member refusal code and as the START state of a re-invite, which is legal only from ReinvitableStatuses = Rejected, Deleted. DEDICATED account: blocked from TechFlow by design.

VCST-5281 status representative — Deleted (a BlockingStatus, and Reinvitable). Completes the four-value legal set so no branch of MembershipStatuses.IsBlocking is left unrepresented by the fixture set. Same single-org shape over an Approved contact. THE POINT: the membership ROW still exists — Deleted is a status value, not a row deletion — which is exactly the distinction this fixture makes observable, and it is why teardown must remove the row rather than trust the status. DEDICATED account: blocked from TechFlow by design.
